title: Deep-learning diagnosis of onychomycosis on histology, non-inferior to pathologists
summary: A deep-learning system trained on annotated fungal elements in nail-clipping histology achieved an AUC of 0.981 on a second dataset of 199 cases, non-inferior to dermatopathologists for specificity and AUC at a 5% margin. The AI struggled with spores and confused serum or aggregated bacteria with fungal elements, needed a large number of training images, and sensitivity is not stated in the abstract. The study is from a single centre.
ai_technology: Deep-learning detection of fungal elements in nail-clipping histopathology images

evidence.tested: Separate second dataset of 199 cases with a comparison against dermatopathologists.
evidence.unknown: Sensitivity; performance at other centres; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning model detected fungal elements in stained nail histology to support diagnosis.
